fields.name: EscalatethecasetoQOS
fields.fieldText:
If the customer is experiencing QoS issues on multiple locations, it would help the escalation team to know who the contact person is for each location. Escalate the case to QOS. Reminders before escalating the case:
  • Ask the customer the contact person of the other locations and their respective contact numbers.
  • Set expectations with the customer regarding their case being escalated.
  • Do not forget to select the correct QoS disposition based on the issue being escalated.
  • Use probing questions to determine if the customer has any other unresolved issues. Take ownership and appropriate action to ensure unresolved issues are handled correctly.
  • Ensure that your case notes are detailed and concise.
  • On the current location that is also experiencing issues, make sure that the information below are included (Note: failure to do so may result to an escalation feedback).
    • Call samples
      • Gather all call samples of when the issue has been encountered.
    • Type of QoS issue
      • Input whether it's audio loss, garbled voice, noise, volume distortion,echoed voice, dropped calls, or audio delay.
      • List all applicable issues if multiple issues exist.
    • Internet service provider
      • Take note of the provider information that was gathered earlier.
    • Network hardware information
      • Modem make and model
      • Router make and model
      • Switch make and model
    • Attached devices to the network
      • # of hardwired computers
      • # of Wi-Fi devices
      • # of IP telephony phones
    • Affected devices
      • User extension : Serial number : Phone model
    • Any programs or devices that may generate internet traffic
      • Cloud backup software
        • Cloud backup is a technology that involves sending a copy of your data to an offsite vendor, a cloud provider, that keeps the data secure and accessible in real time. It's important to take note as this technology may saturate the customer's internet connection at certain intervals causing QoS issues.
        • Examples of cloud backup software are:
          • Carbonite
          • Crashplan
          • Google Drive
          • Dropbox
          • Box
      • IP Cameras or DVRs that have video streaming capabilities
        • IP cameras or DVRs that can stream live and archived video to mobile phones and computers through the internet that may also saturate the customer's internet connection and cause quality orf service issues..
    • Speedtest results
      • Run a speedtest from the customer's network by going to speedtest.net and take note of the following:
        • Ping
        • Download speed
        • Upload speed
        • Test result code (have the customer click SHARE THIS RESULT)
    • Additional information
      • Date the issue started.
      • Were there changes on the network before this issue started? (Yes or No)
Click NEXT to add notes to an existing case or to create a new case for this issue

fields.name: Identifyingtheservicebeingused
fields.fieldText:
Identifying the service being used. Part of providing the resolution to the QoS issue is identifying the type of service the customer is using when they encounter the problem. RingCentral offers different types of telephony services and each service requires a different approach to resolving a call quality issue. IP PHONE
  • An IP Phone is a telephony device assigned to the DigitalLine.
  • These phones have the same features as a regular analog phone, if not, more.
SOFTPHONE (RINGCENTRAL FOR DESKTOP)
  • RingCentral for Desktop is an easy-to-use app, and a comprehensive communications hub with all-inclusive phone, fax, business SMS, and conferencing for your desktop.
  • It provides an intuitive interface that optimizes user experience and increases productivity.
  • It can be installed on both PCs and Macs.
MOBILE APPLICATION (RINGCENTRAL MOBILE APP FOR IOS AND ANDROID)
  • The RingCentral Mobile App empowers the user to take voice, fax, text, HD video meetings, and conferencing with them anywhere, anytime, on their mobile devices.
  • It can be installed on both IOS and Android platforms.
REGULAR FORWARDING NUMBER
  • Regular forwarding numbers refer to non-RingCentral numbers where the users intend to route the call.
  • These numbers can point to landline telephones, mobile phone, and answering services.
RINGOUT
  • RingOut enables one-touch calling from any phone or internet-enabled computer.
  • When using RingOut, RingCentral contacts the caller first then connects the caller to the desired recipient.
  • There are a few ways to use the RingOut feature. Users can initiate a RingOut call from:
    • RingCentral online account
    • RingCentral Desktop Application
    • RingCentral Mobile Appliication
    • RingCentral Integration for SalesForce, Microsoft Outlook, or Google Chrome
WEBRTC (RINGCENTRAL FOR GOOGLE CHROME / MICROSOFT OUTLOOK)
  • WebRTC is a technology which supports browser-to-browser applications for voice calling, video chat, and [peer-to-peer] P2P file sharing without the need of either internal or external plugins.
  • RingCentral supports voice communications directly from Google Chrome or Microsoft Outlook using the computer's microphone.

fields.name: Issueidentification
fields.fieldText:
Issue identification. QoS issues vary depending on the symptoms customers are reporting. Here, we'll be categorizing each symptom so we can properly identify the issue. The symptoms are categorized as: AUDIO LOSS
  • Absolute Silence
    • Symptom: This type of silence can be understood if you ever had the experience of not knowing whether the other person is still there because there is no sound on the line. Neither the caller or the callee can hear each other.
  • One-way Audio
    • Symptom: This can be understood in a situation wherein one party can be heard, but the other party cannot hear the audio coming in the opposite direction. In other wiords, the caller can hear the callee but the callee cannot hear the caller (or vice versa).
  • Sporadic Audio loss
    • Symptom: This can be understood in a situation wherein both parties are engaged to a conversation then suddenly one or the other loses audio for a significant amount of time. The call timer is still active on both parties indicating that the call is still active.
GARBLED VOICE
  • Choppy Voice / Clipped Voice
    • Symptom: Choppy voice describes the sound when there are gaps in the voice during a conversation. Syllables appear to be dropped or badly delayed in a start and stop fashion. Most customers describe this type of problem as if the audio is "cutting in and out".
  • Robotic Voice
    • Symptom: This is the kind of problem when the voice during a conversation may sound robotic or synthesized.
  • Underwater Voice
    • Symptom: This voice problem is similar to the sound of your voice when heard underwater.
  • Tunnel Voice
    • Symptom: This is the type of audio problem when either the caller or the callee sounds as if he or she is talking inside a tunnel.
NOISE
  • Clicking / Popping
    • Symptom: Clicking is an external sound similar to knocking that is inserted usually at intervals.
  • Crackling
    • Symptom: Crackling is an irregular form of very light static noice that is similar to the sound a fire makes.
  • Crosstalk
    • Symptom: This type of noise describes the concept when the customer hears another conversation on the line. Commonly, the other party can't hear the customer however there are forms when all parties hear each other.
  • Hissing
    • Symptom: Hissing is the noise being heard and is often associated to the term "white noise". This noise is often constant throughout the conversation.
  • Humming / Buzzing
    • Symptom: This type of noise is the buzzing sound you hear that is similar to the sound heard on a radio when a nearby mobile phone is about to be called or detecting a cell.
  • Static
    • Symptom: Static is a very common problem that describes the noise being heard when the radio has a bad reception.
VOLUME DISTORTION
  • Fluctuating Voice
    • Symptom: Fluctuating voice is when the volume of the voice increases and decreases in a wave fashion.
  • Fuzzy Voice
    • Symptom: Fuzzy voice sounds similar to a radio turned up too loud and the voice is shaky.
  • Muffled Voice
    • Symptom: Muffled voice sounds similar to when you speak with your hand over your mouth.
ECHOED VOICE
  • SymptomListener Echo
    • Symptom: This type of echo is described when the listener hears the talker twice.
  • Talker Echo
    • Symptom: Talker echo is similar to listener echo but it's when the talker hears an echo of his or her own voice.
DROPPED CALLS
  • Symptom: Dropped calls is caused by a problem which, due to technical reasons, disconnects the active call before the speaking parties had finished their conversation and before one of them had the chance to hang up.
AUDIO DELAY
  • Symptom: Audio delay is a problem characterized by the latency experienced during the time it takes for speech to exit the speaker’s mouth and reach the listener’s ear. Often, the latency causes the caller and callee to talk over each other.

fields.name: ProblemwiththeWiFiconnection
fields.fieldText:
Problem with the Wi-Fi connection. If the QoS issue is not encountered when the computer is hardwired to the modem or router, this means that there is an issue with the computer's Wi-Fi connection.
  • Use probing questions to determine if the customer has any other unresolved issues. Take ownership and appropriate action to ensure unresolved issues are handled correctly.
Below are a few tips to improve the customer's Wi-Fi connection.
  • Reboot the computer and the wireless router
    • Try unplugging the router for 5 to 10 seconds and then plugging it back in.
    • This technique of powercycling your router is a tried-and-true method for restoring a previously functional wireless network to good working order.
  • Change the Wi-Fi channel on the router
    • Most Wi-Fi routers and devices use the 2.4GHz radio band which has 11 channels. Unfortunately, only 3 of the 11 channels can run simultaneously without overlapping or interfering with each other. Many routers are set to broadcast on channel 6 by default. Interference from other routers in the vicinity is a common source of connectivity problems.
    • Many routers have an automatic channel selection feature. This can be disabled and the user can manually choose a channel. For maximum performance, it's best to stick with channel 1 or 11. Once changed, have the customer reconnect and then check to see whether your connectivity problem persists.
  • Check and reposition the wireless router
    • Make sure that the router's antennas are securely attached and are positioned upright.
    • Ensure that the router is not blocked behind large objects that might cause the signal to degrade faster.
    • For best results, place the router out in the open so the signal can travel freely.

fields.name: Thetypeofinternetconnection
fields.fieldText:
The type of internet connection plays a significant role in determining why the customer is experiencing QoS issues. A connection that is stable and consistent in performance is required to ensure good voice quality. It is recommended to have a high-speed DSL, cable or fiber connection with enough bandwidth to accommodate both regular internet traffic and the required number of simultaneous voice calls. A connection with a business-level service agreement is preferable, though not required. Ask the customer what type of internet connection they use for VOIP. Most of the customers know the type of internet connection they are using, but in the event that they dont, you can help narrow down the type of connection they are using based on the information below: TYPE A
  • DSL
    • DSL stands for Digital Subscriber Line. Users get a high speed bandwidth connection from a phone wall jack on an existing telephone network. DSL works within the frequencies that the telephone doesn’t utilize so you can use the Internet while making phone calls.
  • Cable
    • Cable provides an internet connection through a cable modem and operates over cable TV lines. Cable provides much greater bandwidth than DSL.
  • Fiber-Optic
    • Optical fiber internet connections or commonly known as fiber internet offer much faster speeds over much longer distances than traditional copper-based technologies like DSL and cable. Fiber optic connections are installed using strong cables with strands of thin optical fibers that transmit beams of light. These fibers, which are contained in a glass or plastic pipe, use the light to send information from point A to point B.
TYPE B Note: These type of connections are unsuitable for VOIP and unsupported by RingCentral.
  • Satellite
    • Satellite accesses the internet via a satellite in Earth’s orbit. The enormous distances that a signal travels from earth to satellite and back again introduces more latency than cable, DSL or fiber.
  • Fixed Wireless Broadband
    • Fixed wireless broadband is a type of high-speed internet access where connections to service providers use radio signals rather than cables or fiber. Service providers provide this type of connection to areas that lack fiber, DSL or cable television lines so users can still enjoy broadband internet access.
  • Mobile Internet
    • Mobile internet provides wireless internet access through cellular phones or hotspot devices. The speeds vary depending on the service provider and plan, but the most common are 3G and 4G speeds. 3G is a term that describes a 3rd generation cellular network obtaining mobile speeds of around 2.0 Mbps while LTE or 4G is the fourth generation of cellular wireless standards. GPRS and Edge offer much lower speeds compared to 3G, 4G / LTE.
  • Dial-up Connection
    • Dial-up internet access is a form of Internet access that uses the facilities of the public switched telephone network (PSTN) to establish a connection to an Internet service provider (ISP) by dialing a telephone number on a conventional telephone line. This type of connection is unsuitable for VOIP and unsupported by RingCentral.

fields.name: Understandingcalldroppingissues
fields.fieldText:
Understanding call dropping issues. Calls dropping are caused by different factors and should be handled accordingly based on the symptoms below. Keep in mind that calls may also be perceived as dropped if the other party hangs up during a conversation experiencing extreme QoS issues. If this happens, reuse the guide not for troubleshooting dropped calls but to troubleshoot the issue based on the call quality problem being encountered.
  • Call duration timer still running
    • Calls maybe perceived as dropped even when the timer is still running. When this happens, this means that the call is still technically ACTIVE and the customer just lost the incoming audio coming from the other party.
        Instances such as this may cause the call to "drop" not because RingCentral disconnected the call, but it's possible that the other party has hung up due to not hearing the customer after some time.
    • When the call duration is still running, it is audio loss being encountered and not calls dropping.
  • Call duration timer stops then the phone goes back to the idle screen
    • When the call duration stops, this indicates that the leg between the caller and the callee was disconnected.
    • There's no way to identify if the call was disconnected by the other party or if it was RingCentral experiencing the issue.
    • If call drops actually do happen, an incorrectly configured network may also be the cause of the problem.
